title.narrative: ERSKI/KIB/The joint OECD-UN-Habitat Cities Connect Initiative

description.narrative: The United Nations Human Settlements Programme (UN-Habitat) and The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) have entered a collaboration to establish the joint OECD-UN-Habitat Cities Connect Initiative. Cities Connect is a global platform that aims to address the development challenges faced by intermediary cities, whilst exploiting the potential of this type of agglomerations for poverty reduction and national development. This initiative is led by the OECD Development Centre and UN-Habitat. This project is attached to the partnership agreement between OECD and UN-Habitat in the area of sustainable urban development to support the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goal 11and the New Urban Agenda. Both the OECD Development Centre and UN-Habitat have been actively engaged with national and local governments to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals and the New Urban Agenda. A continuous dialogue with key stakeholders engaged in urban development has shown that policy actions that trigger the development of intermediary cities have not only become an evident but a pressing need. Although this is an issue that starts to emerge among policy discussion circles, there is only a very limited number of organizations and institutions working with intermediary cities. Moreover, most of these initiatives follow a network structure, which certainly provides its participants with practical information on experiences for addressing common challenges. However, there is no single platform that defragments and generates new knowledge regarding the multi-dimensional challenges faced by intermediary cities in a structured and coherent way. The OECD Development Centre and UN-Habitat held a meeting in April 2018 with international experts on urban development, in order to advance with the agenda and discuss the multiple roles played by intermediary cities in development processes, as well as to identify the main challenges and opportunities they face. The following was identified: 1. intermediary cities play a key role for poverty reduction and economic development. Nevertheless, additional empirical evidence is needed to identify the channels through which agglomeration economies emerged in intermediary cities, how rural-urban linkages lead to economic transformation and employment creation, and how policy actions be more effective. 2. tapping the potential of intermediary cities, and addressing their challenges, requires a territorial approach and better coordination among different levels of government. Moreover, it further requires analyzing the interaction between municipalities and central governments in financial terms. 3. there is a pressing need for a new and conducive financial system that allows intermediary cities to access resources and provide infrastructure and basic services to growing populations. 4. complementary and participatory involvement will be required to address the different types of challenges faced by intermediary cities.
